extracted.intended_audience: Investigators preparing NIH R01 (human subjects, inclusion, recruitment, and vertebrate animals) application sections
extracted.subtask_description: Filling the human subjects, inclusion (children/women/minorities), recruitment/retention, protection of subjects, and vertebrate animal use sections of an NIH R01 application, ensuring compliance with applicable regulations and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Questionnaire / Trial Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the study involve human participants? Are participants prospectively assigned to an intervention? Is the study designed to evaluate the effect of the intervention on the participants? Is the effect a health-related biomedical or behavioral outcome? Provide the ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answers to these items determine whether the project is an NIH-defined clinical trial and whether a ClinicalTrials.gov registration (NCT number) is required. Respond with Yes/No and include identifier (e.g., NCT87654321) when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Individuals Across the Lifespan (Children Inclusion Policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans to include children (as defined by the NIH Policy on Inclusion of Children) with scientific and ethical rationale for age range selected; state explicit age inclusion/exclusion (here: include 6 months–18 years; exclude <6 months due to maternal IgG interference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justification for age limits, address Additional Protections for Children (45 CFR Part 46 Subpart D), describe assent process for children able to assent, and show that facilities and investigator expertise are appropriate for pediatric research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women and Minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement that the study will be inclusive of all eligible subjects regardless of religion, sex, or ethnic background; provide targeted/planned enrollment by race, ethnicity, and sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a Targeted/Planned Enrollment Table with anticipated percentages/numbers (e.g., 55% females, 45% males) and report how local demographics informed estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment Plan and Subject Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods to identify potential subjects (e.g., daily contact with clinical services, microbiology lab notifications, electronic algorithms such as Sentri7®) and specific inclusion/exclusion criteria for screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe operational workflow (who screens, how notifications occur), explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., polymicrobial infection, immune compromise, recent IVIG, pregnancy), and attachments (Protection of Human Subjects) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategies to maximize retention: clear communication of timeline/expectations, aligning study visits and blood draws with routine care, reimbursement for time/travel, flexible scheduling, and collecting multiple contact methods for follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain concrete retention tactics (e.g., reimbursing participants, flexible times, using routine-care blood draws to minimize extra sticks) and follow-up contact procedures for late visits (~6 months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed Consent and Assent Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All participating subjects must sign an informed consent form that complies with 21 CFR Part 50 and 45 CFR 46; assent from children when able; consent process is initiated prior to participation and continues throughout study involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent/assent forms must be IRB-approved, contain no exculpatory statements, provide comprehensive explanation of procedures/risks/PHI use, offer sufficient time to consider participation, and copies of signed forms must be given to participants. Use age-appropriate assent scripts for younger children (3–6 years verbal/scripted; 7–17 years assent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects — Confidentiality and Data Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Data will be stored de-identified with unique subject IDs; access limited to PI, key study personnel, and IRB; database (REDCap) must be secure, HIPAA- and FISMA-compliant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State who has access, how data are de-identified, limits on use of data, and allowed disclosures (public domain, IRB review, necessary medical care, or publication). Describe electronic safeguards and that only key personnel will access patient charts and REDCap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk Minimization and Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize risks to subjects (here: minimal risk limited to blood draws with possible local/systemic venipuncture reactions); state that no investigational products are used and study results will not guide clinical care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific measures to minimize risk (timing blood draws with routine care, limiting volumes), and explicit statements that subjects may opt out of blood draws and that participation will not change clinical care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blood Draw Volume Limits and Sampling Schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified blood draw volumes and timing: up to two 10 mL tubes (20 mL total) per sampling, and no more than 1.0 ml/kg if subject <20 kg; samples at enrollment (within 1 day), 4–6 weeks (convalescent), ~6 months (late convalescent, window 5–7 months), and optionally 1–3 years for selected subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare exact collection volumes, maximums per weight, number and timing of draws, and justify that volumes meet minimal risk descriptions. Note optional long-term sampling criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vulnerable Subjects Protections (Children)
rubrics_metrics.description: When children are the only vulnerable population included, address why inclusion is necessary, expertise of the team, facilities, and additional protections under 45 CFR Part 46 Subpart D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide investigator qualifications, facility description (e.g., freestanding children's hospital capacity), sample size justification for children, assent procedures, and safeguards to minimize risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Collection Methods and Source Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical data collection from electronic medical records (EpicLeap) including demographics, diagnoses, culture results, fever duration/height, and lab values; access restricted to PI and key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe exact data elements to be extracted, the electronic systems used, personnel roles for chart access, and linkage to specimen IDs to maintain confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Compliance: IRB, Single IRB, and Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether the study is multi-site using the same protocol and whether a Single IRB plan is attached; provide Inclusion Enrollment Reports and OMB-category racial/ethnic reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach Single IRB plan when applicable, supply required Inclusion Enrollment Report entries (location, domestic/foreign), and use OMB-specified race/ethnicity categories in reporting planned/actual enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring (DSM) / DSMB Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate existence of a Data and Safety Monitoring Plan and whether a Data and Safety Monitoring Board will be appointed for the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State overall DSM structure, frequency of reviews, who oversees safety, and whether an independent DSMB is required (answer Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Timeline and Milestones (Aims and Sample Collection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed timeline: recruitment start (onset of award), enrollment duration, timing for each Aim (e.g., Aim 1 during years 1–4; Aim 2 years 2–4; Aim 3 year 1 through final year), and schedule for sample collection windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a general schematic with start/stop dates, coordination of enrollment and experimental aims, and when sample collections and follow-ups occur relative to enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome Measures and Statistical Design
rubrics_metrics.description: List outcome measures (type, name, time frame, brief description) and describe statistical design and power, subject participation duration, and whether FDA-regulated interventions are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide primary/secondary outcome definitions with time frames, sample size/power calculations, expected duration per subject, and if FDA-regulated interventions are involved, describe IP/IND/IDE status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Field to describe how study results will be disseminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans for publication, data sharing, and reporting results to participants or the public as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals Use Description and Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description of proposed animal experiments (species/strains, group sizes per experiment, total numbers), justification for animal model (e.g., mice standard for S. aureus studies), and IACUC protocol reference/approval status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numbers per aim (here: examples: Aim1 2400 mice, Aim2 1800+30, Aim3 etc., total ~5890), explain scientific necessity, and include IACUC protocol number and approval status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of Pain, Distress, and Euthanasia Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe procedures to minimize pain/distress (anesthesia with isoflurane, euthanasia when animals unthrifty), and specify euthanasia methods consistent with AVMA guidelines (isoflurane inhalation followed by cervical dislocation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State anesthesia and monitoring plans, humane endpoints, personnel experience, and adherence to AVMA panel recommendations for euthanasia to assure death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and Select Agent Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: State whether the proposal uses select agents (here: does not) and confirm that S. aureus infection experiments will adhere to BSL2 guidelines and be conducted by staff with BSL2 training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare select agent status, appropriate biosafety level for work, staff training requirements, and institutional biosafety approvals/oversight.
